extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media organisations, policymakers, and Press Council members
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations, procedural standards, and ethical criteria for safeguarding press freedom, adjudicating complaints against authorities and the press, and supporting journalistic practice in Jammu & Kashmir and India more broadly. Includes operational, welfare, and procedural norms the Press Council expects stakeholders to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police spokespersons appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Police requires additional spokespersons, these should be appointed, but they should not represent other departments by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate spokespeople specifically for police communications rather than using officials who also represent other departments; avoid default assignment of multi-departmental representatives to police spokesperson roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore rights and privileges of the Kashmir Press Club
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kashmir Press Club was a registered representative body; its registration was 'de-registered' and its legal existence held 'in abeyance' despite prior re-registration. Representative bodies of journalists should be allowed to function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FFC recommends that the registration of the Kashmir Press Club should be restored and government officials should not interfere in the election process of what is essentially a private body of news persons; in a democracy journalist bodies' views should be sought and respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry norms for digital networks
rubrics_metrics.description: A large number of digital channels and media networks on platforms like Facebook and Twitter have sprung up with no entry barrier or oversight to ensure they observe basic norms of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out a survey and registration process for these news platforms by neutral, autonomous bodies (e.g., Indian Readership Survey, BARC) so that both legal due diligence and journalistic ethics are observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for Urdu publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Several government departments had suspended the purchase of Urdu publications and Urdu publications were handicapped in allotment of government advertising due to shortage of DIPR officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restore government subscriptions to Urdu publications, remedy DIPR staffing shortages, and restore advertising support to ensure balance with other language publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance and health cover for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Jammu and Kashmir is a conflict zone where journalists risk life and limb; a 2018 scheme for medical and accident cover was worked out but not implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Union Territory government should take the initiative to implement the medical and accident cover scheme financed by the state at the earliest to protect journalists' welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation access (district level)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2017 FFC recommendations proposed that accreditation for journalists should be extended to the district level; since 1 April 2020 no accreditation has been given in the Union Territory, blocking access to news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend and resume accreditation at district level to ensure journalists have necessary access for news gathering; avoid administrative lapses that prevent accreditation issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and powers in Media Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Media Policy of 2020 contained provisions considered to give government machinery powers 'as both judge and prosecutors' and had committees without journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media policies should include journalist representation on committees and avoid concentrating adjudicatory and regulatory powers in government machinery that could undermine press freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure free flow of information—internet and facilitation centres
rubrics_metrics.description: Cutting off the Internet (e.g., August 2019) and restrictive gateways/Media Facilitation Centre arrangements hindered transmission of news and deliberately stopped free flow of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities and facilities intended to assist journalists must not create gateways or restrictive regimes that impede transmission of news; ensure infrastructure and policies enable unhindered information flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using facilities/advertising/accreditation to control editorial stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities responsible for providing facilities (advertisements, accreditation) sometimes use them as a means to control the editorial stance of newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbitrary or improper denial of advertisements or accreditation that affects financial viability or access is impermissible; such facilities must not be weaponized to influence editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suomotu action procedure (Regulations 13/5/14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council, through its Chairperson, has power to take Suo‑Motu action in matters of grave significance under Regulation 13; thereafter procedure from Regulation 5 onwards shall be followed as if it were a complaint under Regulation 14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When initiating Suo‑Motu inquiries follow the prescribed procedural sequence (Regulation 5 onwards) equivalent to formal complaints under Regulation 14 to ensure due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication outcome categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes used by the Council for adjudicated matters are categorised as: Upheld; Dropped; Assurance/Settled/Amends; Dropped for Non‑pursuance/Sub‑judice/Withdrawal/Lack of Substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these discrete labels to report adjudication results consistently; statistical analyses of cases should classify each adjudication into one of these outcome types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council's statutory mandate (Section 13, Press Council Act, 1978)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council is entrusted to safeguard freedom of the press and enhance standards of newspapers and news agencies; it monitors developments that may restrict availability and dissemination of news in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudications, monitoring, and recommendations should be driven by the objectives in Section 13: preserve press freedom, improve standards, and ensure public interest news is not impeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles on corrections and right of reply
rubrics_metrics.description: To err is human; a quick correction is the best remedy. When the aggrieved sends a contradiction or rejoinder, editors must publish it with due promptitude and prominence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should promptly and prominently publish corrections and rejoinders to uphold right of reply and mitigate reputational harm; reluctance to publish contradicting material violates salutary principles of journalistic conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and reporting statistical categories for complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council records categories of complainants and respondents (e.g., English press, Indian languages press, newspaper associations, journalists, police/government authorities, information department, institutions/private companies, private persons, suo‑motu) and statewise distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain systematic categorical and statewise statistical records of complaints and adjudications to identify trends and focus remedial measures; use the categories consistently in annual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication as a means to evolve journalistic conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Through adjudications and guidelines derived from court pronouncements and institutional precedents, the Council builds a code of conduct for the press to adhere to while performing duties within ethical boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use case‑by‑case adjudications and published pronouncements to develop and clarify ethical standards and expectations for the press; treat adjudications as precedent-informing instruments for elevating standards.
